# Casa Amani Madeira

> Made for slow stays on Madeira's quiet side.

Casa Amani is a two-bedroom contemporary rental villa in Arco da Calheta, on the south-west coast of Madeira, Portugal. The house sits split-level above a private pool with a front-facing sea view (pool heating available at extra cost), and is designed for slow stays, equally suited to travellers visiting Madeira, to remote-mobile workers using the island as a base, and to surfers based on the island's west-coast breaks. It sleeps up to six and is available for stays of one week or longer. Registered Alojamento Local 176882/AL.

## Property details

- Location: Arco da Calheta, Calheta municipality, Madeira, Portugal
- Coordinates: 32.715988, -17.140852
- Architecture: split-level contemporary, 219 m2 on a 324 m2 plot
- Bedrooms: 2 (two king beds; the guest bedroom king can split into two singles)
- Lower level: two additional single beds for a fifth and sixth guest
- Bathrooms: 3 (en-suite to the main bedroom, family bathroom on the main level, one on the lower level)
- Pool: private 7 m pool with panoramic sea view; heating available at extra cost
- Sea view: yes, front-facing from the main level
- Parking: private garage for two cars, directly connected to the house
- Check-in: 16:00 via smart lock (access codes shared 48 hours before arrival)
- Check-out: 11:00
- Minimum stay: 7 nights
- Pets: not allowed
- Smoking: not allowed
- Time zone: GMT/WET (same as London; UTC+0 in winter, UTC+1 in summer)
- Touristic licence: Alojamento Local 176882/AL
- Managed by: OurMadeira (Cessao de Exploracao contract)

## The main bedroom

King bed facing the Atlantic, with an en-suite bathroom and a desk behind the bed for early work or reading. The window wall looks out over the pool to the ocean.

## The guest bedroom

King bed just off the living space, with a built-in desk and external monitor for both rest and remote work. The king can be split into two single mattresses on request.

## The family bathroom

Microcement throughout, with a rain shower and built-in Bluetooth sound. Warm, soft, and easy to use day to day.

## The living space

Open-plan living with direct access to the terrace and pool, where most of the day moves between inside and out.

## The kitchen

Fully equipped: induction hob, oven, microwave, dishwasher, espresso machine, toaster, kettle. Used daily from morning coffee to longer meals later on.

## The lower room

Downstairs room with two single beds and its own bathroom. More private and comfortable, though without a window.

## The outdoor dining area

Outdoor table and gas barbecue set just beyond the living space. Meals tend to move outside without much planning.

## The west coast

Most visitors to Madeira stay in Funchal or along the south-east coast. The west side, from Ribeira Brava to Porto Moniz, is where the island opens up. Fewer hotels, fewer tour buses, longer views. The south-west coast gets more sun hours than anywhere else on the island, sheltered from the north-east trade winds by the central mountain range.

Calheta municipality is the heart of this stretch. Its marina has one of the island's only sand beaches. Jardim do Mar, ten minutes downhill, is a recognised surf break. Paul do Mar, further along the coast, is quieter still.

## Climate

Madeira's south-west coast is mild year-round. Summer averages 22 to 26 degrees Celsius; winter rarely drops below 16 degrees. Rain falls mostly on the north side and in the mountains; the south-west is the dry side. The sea temperature ranges from 18 degrees in winter to 24 degrees in summer, warm enough for swimming most of the year.

## Getting here

Madeira International Airport (FNC) has direct flights year-round from London, Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Paris, Lisbon, Porto, Warsaw, and a dozen other European cities. Low-cost carriers (easyJet, Ryanair, Wizz Air) and full-service airlines (TAP, British Airways, Condor) both serve the island. From the airport, Arco da Calheta is about 50 minutes west along the VR1 motorway. A hire car is recommended.

## Golf on Madeira

Madeira has three eighteen-hole courses. Palheiro Golf sits above Funchal on the south coast, designed by Cabell Robinson. Santo da Serra Golf, designed by Robert Trent Jones Sr., hosts the Madeira Open. Porto Santo Golf, designed by Seve Ballesteros, occupies the neighbouring island. From Arco da Calheta, Palheiro and Santo da Serra are forty-five to fifty minutes by car.

## Surfing west Madeira

The west coast faces the open Atlantic with consistent swells year-round. Three recognised breaks sit within fifteen minutes of the house: Jardim do Mar (right-hand point break, intermediate to advanced), Paul do Mar (powerful right-hander, experienced surfers), and Ponta Pequena (left-hand reef break, less crowded). Water temperature ranges from 18 degrees in February to 24 degrees in September. A 3/2mm wetsuit is standard year-round.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Where exactly is Casa Amani?
A: In Arco da Calheta, a village on the south-west coast of Madeira island, Portugal. About 50 minutes by car from Madeira International Airport (FNC).

Q: How many people does it sleep?
A: Up to six. Two king beds plus two single beds on the lower level.

Q: Is there a pool?
A: Yes. A private 7-metre pool set into the terrace, facing the Atlantic. Heating is available at extra cost.

Q: Is it suitable for remote work?
A: Yes. Both bedrooms have a desk. The guest bedroom has an external monitor. Fibre Wi-Fi throughout. GMT/WET time zone overlaps with the UK, most of Europe, and the US East Coast morning.

Q: What is the minimum stay?
A: Seven nights.

Q: Are pets allowed?
A: No.

Q: Is there air conditioning?
A: Air conditioning throughout the house. The same units can be set to heat when needed.

Q: How do I book?
A: Through Airbnb. All "Stay with us" buttons on the site link to the Airbnb listing.

Q: Is breakfast included?
A: No. The house is self-catering. The kitchen is fully equipped. A private chef can be arranged on request.

Q: Do I need a car?
A: Yes, for most things. Car hire on the island is straightforward and affordable.
